_comment: Model configurations for the agent bench. Secrets never live here: each
entry names the environment variable its key comes from, and switch.sh
refuses to run if that variable is unset.
api_base empty  -> first-party Anthropic (Max subscription or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
vision false    -> the main model cannot see images, so screenshots are
routed through the vision describer instead.

pricing is per MILLION tokens, from the provider's published rates. The SDK's total_cost_usd is computed at ANTHROPIC rates whatever model is behind the gateway, so it is meaningless for anything else -- it overstated a deepseek run by 37x. compare.py recomputes cost from these numbers.

vision_describer._why:
Chosen on ACCURACY, not price. The describer costs ~$0.0001 against a $1.87 turn, so cheapness is the wrong objective -- a wrong description makes the main model change code for a screen it never saw.
Verified on real screenshots: reads time and date correctly, names the actual artwork (planet, rocket, stars), and reports the stock 'Install an app to continue' screen.
Rejected: google/gemma-3-12b-it read the time correctly but hallucinated the scene ('a yellow bird with a red beak', 'hills or mounds of green' for a space scene). qwen/qwen3.8-max and openai/gpt-5-nano are mandatory-reasoning and returned no text at all -- they spend the whole budget thinking. google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite also passed and is free, a good fallback.

claude._notes: Subscription auth via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN already on the VM.

kimi._notes: Direct from Moonshot. Use this rather than kimi-or: OpenRouter reported cache_creation_input_tokens=0, so every turn re-sent ~100k uncached input.

kimi-or._notes: Kept for comparison. Also dropped long generations mid-stream: 'API Error: stream closed before completion'.

deepseek._notes: Text only. DeepSeek's API rejects image content outright, so screenshots go through the vision describer.
